title: Exact defect decomposition and compatibility bounds for the Zeta23 rank-trace certificate

claims.statement: The multiplicity-aware rank-trace defect equals a sum of six nonnegative terms: the Schur-transfer defect, positive-range overlap, negative-part matching error, below-threshold overlap, positive-eigenvalue quantization error, and unused positive-inertia budget.
Two certificates at the same parameter satisfy a quantitative compatibility lower bound controlled by the separation of their thresholded positive parts minus the separation of their negative parts.

The orthogonal five-atom model diag(1,1,1,1,2), Q=0 simultaneously saturates the c=2 simple-zero and c=3 distinct-zero scalar inequalities, so merely combining those two scalar inequalities cannot improve the 2/3 and 5/6 constants.

validation.expected: exact no-go assertions pass; all random identity and compatibility residuals are below 2e-8

next_frontier: Prove or refute a two-window separation estimate for actual Weil/Gabor zeta compressions that makes the dual-compression compatibility lower bound macroscopically positive.
cannot_imply: This attempt does not improve any unconditional zeta-zero proportion.
This attempt does not prove or refute the Riemann hypothesis.
Random numerical tests do not establish the candidate theorem.
The algebraic defect identity alone does not show that genuine zeta compressions have positive aggregate defect.
No claim is repository-verified before an isolated independent-verifier run returns PASS on the frozen artifact hashes.
